review: AWAITING CLINICIAN REVIEW. MEDICAL_REVIEW_3 items G1 to G3. These lines are ours, not CDC's, so none shows until a doctor signs off and this is set to true.
notes: One measurement says less than how a baby's measurements move over time. Your baby's doctor can tell you what these mean for your baby.
If your baby was born early, your doctor may look at this differently. This chart counts age from the birth date.
Measurements taken at home can differ from the ones taken at the doctor's office.

lines.text: The World Health Organization (WHO) Child Growth Standards are recommended for plotting and tracking growth of US children from birth to 2 years.
lines.source: CDC, Using WHO Growth Standard Charts

lines.text: Percentile curves show the distribution of selected body measurements in children.
lines.source: CDC, Overview of CDC Growth Charts

after_two.text: At age 2 years, CDC recommends transitioning to the CDC Growth Charts.
